cultivar: Yueyang local landrace and Fuding Dabai
processing: A bud with one or two leaves is pan-fired, piled briefly to yellow while warm, lightly rolled, then dried in stages; a light yellowing in the 'yellow small tea' style.
harvest_season: Spring, from late March to late April; pre-Qingming and yu qian lots.
appearance_dry: Slightly curled, downy shoots in yellow-green with golden tips.
appearance_wet: Tender yellow-green bud-and-leaf sets, even and soft.
taste_profile: Mellow and sweet with chestnut and a light floral note, a soft round body and a clean, gentle finish.

brewing.notes: Gaiwan or glass at 80–85 °C. A gentle bud tea; four steeps, with the first two carrying most of the flavour.

vintage_note: Sold as the current year's spring harvest in pre-Qingming and yu qian lots, mostly within Hunan and usually for far less than Junshan Yinzhen. Drink within the year, kept cold and sealed.
description:
Beigang Mao Jian is a yellow tea from Beigang in Yueyang, Hunan, in the Dongting Lake country that also gives Junshan Silver Needle. It belongs to the 'yellow small tea' group, bud-with-leaf teas given a light yellowing, and it is the plainer, more affordable relative of the island's famous tea.

The leaf is pan-fired, then piled briefly while still warm so it yellows a little, rolled lightly and dried in stages. The yellowing is light, so the tea sits closer to a mellow green than to a fully yellowed bud tea, with a golden tint rather than a golden colour.

In the cup it is mellow and sweet, chestnut and a light floral note, a soft round body and a clean gentle finish, with the grassy edge of a green bud tea sanded off. It takes 80–85 °C in a gaiwan and gives four steeps. It is not a dramatic tea; it is a pleasant daily one.

It is sold as the spring crop of the current year in pre-Qingming and yu qian lots, mostly within Hunan, and it is usually cheap. Bought under its own name it is good value. Check for a yellow-green rather than green leaf and a mellow rather than grassy smell.
history:
Beigang Mao Jian is a yellow tea from Beigang in Yueyang, Hunan, and from Kangwang township in Yueyang county. The name people usually attach to its deep past is Yonghu tea (邕湖茶), the Tang dynasty name for tea from this area. By the Qianlong reign of the Qing dynasty it already had a reputation.

It is classed among the 'small yellow teas', with Wei Shan Mao Jian and Yuan'an Lu Yuan. Little is documented in detail about how its making changed, or about who made it known.
